bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material availability and input cost volatility tied to geopolitics — Geopolitical tensions in West Asia disrupted the availability and pricing of key inputs including ammonia and crude-linked derivatives during FY 2025-26, and temporary ammonia shortages directly slowed the ramp-up of the new Sayakha methylamines facility. Management states it remains watchful of elevated crude and input costs arising from the West Asia situation, which support API realisations but can moderate domestic demand in the antibiotic category.
- API price pressure and subdued domestic antibiotic demand — Domestic demand for antibiotics remained subdued through FY 2025-26 while raw material and energy costs stayed elevated; the first half was described as particularly testing, with pricing pressures weighing on profitability. Antibiotics are the largest therapeutic exposure at 37.4% of FY 2025-26 revenue, so demand and realisation swings in that category are structurally material.
- Execution and utilisation risk on newly commissioned greenfield capacity — Start-up costs at newly commissioned facilities weighed on first-half profitability, and installed capacity expanded 35% to 82,512 MT in FY 2025-26 while production rose only 18%. The Sayakha methylamines plant was at just over 40% utilisation at March 2026, and the Tarapur Salicylic Acid plant halted production in Q4 pending phenol recovery equipment because it was operating below variable cost recovery. Returns depend on converting this headroom into output.
- Regulatory approval and compliance dependence across multiple jurisdictions — Access to the Company's highest-value markets is gated by USFDA, UK MHRA, EU GMP, ANVISA and COFEPRIS approvals on named facilities, and by DMF and dossier clearances. The regulated-market share of revenue rose to 73% in FY 2025-26, so the business is increasingly dependent on maintaining these accreditations; the AR notes one plant was refurbished specifically to meet stringent standards for upcoming European regulatory audits. The Company also lists Regulatory Compliance as a material governance topic.
- Export and geographic concentration — Exports account for approximately 38% of turnover and the Company serves over 100 countries; the formulations business derives nearly two-thirds of its revenue from exports. This creates structural exposure to trade tariffs, freight and shipping-route disruption (the AR cites disruptions from the Strait of Hormuz to the Red Sea and Suez Canal driving energy and freight costs higher) and to currency and country credit risk, which the Company manages through trade credit insurance and customer credit assessment.
- Climate change, energy and emissions exposure — Identified in the BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table as both risk and opportunity: the Company recognises potential operational and manufacturing losses due to climate-related events, alongside opportunities for innovation and resource efficiency. Mitigation is through climate resilience strategies and initiatives to reduce the carbon footprint. Energy costs also remained elevated through FY 2025-26.
- Environmental compliance burden — water, wastewater and hazardous waste — Water and Wastewater Management and Waste and Hazardous Materials Management are named BRSR material topics for this API and speciality-chemicals manufacturer. Effluent cost is one of the four workstreams in the Tarapur salicylic acid improvement programme, illustrating that environmental treatment cost is a direct determinant of plant economics rather than a peripheral compliance item.
- Key-person and leadership transition risk — Shri Prakash Moreshwar Patil, promoter and Chairman, Managing Director & CEO, takes early retirement with effect from close of business on September 30, 2026, and Whole-time Director Shri Uday Moreshwar Patil retires by rotation at the 41st AGM without seeking re-appointment. The Board is retaining the outgoing Chairman as Management/Technical Consultant for five years specifically to provide guidance and facilitate a smooth transition, and succession planning is an explicit criterion in the Board's own performance evaluation.
- Rising employee attrition — Turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 18.71% in FY 2025-26 from 9.38% in FY 2024-25 and 9.08% in FY 2023-24 — roughly a doubling in one year — in a business whose competitive position rests on process know-how, R&D capability and regulated-market quality systems.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY 2025-26 marked the completion of Aarti Drugs' multi-year investment cycle, with two greenfield facilities commissioned and installed capacity expanding 35% during the year to 82,512 MT while production rose 18% to 53,139 MT; the Company describes the resulting headroom as the principal source of operating leverage available over the medium term. At Sayakha, Gujarat, the greenfield methylamines facility moved from trial to commercial production on September 4, 2025 and, after temporary ammonia shortages linked to the West Asia conflict slowed the ramp, entered a more stable operating phase by March 2026 at a run-rate of approximately 1,000 tonnes per month, representing over 40% utilisation; management expects it to progress towards utilisation above 70% over the coming year, supported by a planned brownfield expansion of an additional 350 TPM of Metformin capacity that will lift captive demand for methylamines. At Tarapur, Maharashtra, the Salicylic Acid plant stabilised at over 300 tonnes per month after addressing initial technology-related challenges, though production was paused in the fourth quarter pending installation of phenol recovery equipment because operating below variable cost recovery served little purpose; a four-part improvement programme covering phenol recovery, effluent cost and an anti-dumping duty application is underway, and the commissioning of a derivatives block is expected to move the facility towards variable cost recovery while providing a platform for forward integration into higher-margin salicylate derivatives. In formulations, the dedicated Oncology Formulation Facility at Baddi, Himachal Pradesh commenced commercial operations and received USFDA approval, EU GMP certification and ANVISA-Brazil approval during the year, with the first oncology product Bicalutamide commercialised; the general Oral Solid Dosage lines became operational for regulated markets following UK MHRA approval and EU GMP certification, and the Company is exploring toll manufacturing to raise utilisation of the specialised oncology infrastructure. The Tarapur API facility was re-approved by the USFDA and a Drug Master File for Metformin was filed with US authorities, with commercial supplies targeted post-validation. Further planned expansion includes a brownfield addition to raise antiprotozoal production capacity by 40%, incremental expansion of chloro-sulphonation facilities, incremental capacity additions and downstream product expansion in the antiprotozoal portfolio, and a greenfield project under evaluation to strengthen the speciality chemicals portfolio. On the energy side, the Company has entered into a Share Subscription and Shareholders' Agreement with Prozeal Green Power Private Limited to develop captive solar power capacity in Gujarat and Maharashtra, with planned solar and wind installations at Sarigam and Tarapur and the solar project expected to commence operations in FY 2026-27; back-pressure turbines are also planned for the co-generation power plant. Capital expenditure over the next few years is planned at Rs 300 Crores to Rs 400 Crores, directed largely towards expansion within adjoining blocks at existing sites, which the Company expects to deliver a higher asset turn than the greenfield phase.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Aarti Drugs Limited is a four-decade-old Indian pharmaceutical manufacturer of active pharmaceutical ingredients, intermediates, speciality chemicals and finished formulations, with a portfolio of over 50 API molecules sold in more than 100 countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Aarti Drugs manufactures and markets active pharmaceutical ingredients, pharmaceutical intermediates and speciality chemicals from integrated plants in Maharashtra and Gujarat, and finished dosage formulations through its wholly owned subsidiary Pinnacle Life Science Private Limited. Its API portfolio spans antibiotics, antiprotozoals, anti-diabetics, anti-inflammatories, antifungals and cardioprotectants, and it describes itself as the largest producer of Metronidazole in India and one of the world's leading producers of Metformin HCl. Customers are pharmaceutical formulation companies, speciality chemical manufacturers and dyes and pigments manufacturers across regulated and semi-regulated markets.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The Company enters FY 2026-27 with its principal investment cycle complete and its focus shifting to utilisation, cost efficiency and mix
- The Sayakha methylamines facility is expected to progress towards utilisation levels above 70% over the coming year, improving captive coverage of critical intermediates for the anti-diabetic portfolio
- At Tarapur, the salicylic acid improvement programme together with the commissioning of the derivatives block is expected to move the facility towards variable cost recovery
- Realisations have stabilised on the demand side, and the share of regulated market business continues to increase, supported by the reapproved US FDA facility, European certifications across several dedicated plants and the Metformin DMF filed with the US FDA
- The formulations business is expected to sustain its recent momentum as approvals convert into commercial supplies, with oncology contributing progressively as dossiers are cleared
- Installed capacity expanded 35% during the year to 82,512 MT following commissioning of two greenfield facilities while production rose 18% to 53,139 MT; the resulting headroom is described as the principal source of operating leverage available over the medium term
- The Company remains watchful of elevated crude and input costs arising from the geopolitical situation in West Asia, which support API realisations while carrying the potential to moderate domestic demand in the antibiotic category
- Taking these factors together, the Company expects a gradual improvement in profitability and return ratios over FY 2026-27 and beyond
- API pricing began to stabilise around September 2025 and strengthened further during the fourth quarter, supported by rising crude prices
- Exports now contribute nearly two-thirds of formulation revenues, reflecting portfolio expansion, a growing pipeline of dossier filings across geographies and regulatory approvals from the USFDA, UK MHRA and European authorities
- The share of revenue from regulated markets increased from 66% in FY 2024-25 to 73% in FY 2025-26
- Domestic demand for antibiotics remained subdued during FY 2025-26 while raw material and energy costs remained elevated; geopolitical tensions in West Asia disrupted availability and pricing of key inputs including ammonia and crude-linked derivatives
- Industry backdrop: the domestic Indian pharmaceutical market is projected by participants to grow 9-11% during FY 2025-26, with chronic therapies, particularly cardiac and anti-diabetic, among the key drivers
- Industry backdrop: India's evolving trade policy framework, including the EU FTA, the UK CETA and the India-New Zealand FTA, is expected to facilitate market access and liberalise tariffs on pharmaceutical products to the advantage of Indian manufacturers
- Industry backdrop: nearly 50% of India's pharmaceutical exports are destined for highly regulated markets, and the industry's stated ambition is USD 50 billion in exports by CY 2030

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2025-26 marked the completion of Aarti Drugs' multi-year investment cycle, with two greenfield facilities commissioned and installed capacity expanding 35% during the year to 82,512 MT while production rose 18% to 53,139 MT; the Company describes the resulting headroom as the principal source of operating leverage available over the medium term. At Sayakha, Gujarat, the greenfield methylamines facility moved from trial to commercial production on September 4, 2025 and, after temporary ammonia shortages linked to the West Asia conflict slowed the ramp, entered a more stable operating phase by March 2026 at a run-rate of approximately 1,000 tonnes per month, representing over 40% utilisation; management expects it to progress towards utilisation above 70% over the coming year, supported by a planned brownfield expansion of an additional 350 TPM of Metformin capacity that will lift captive demand for methylamines. At Tarapur, Maharashtra, the Salicylic Acid plant stabilised at over 300 tonnes per month after addressing initial technology-related challenges, though production was paused in the fourth quarter pending installation of phenol recovery equipment because operating below variable cost recovery served little purpose; a four-part improvement programme covering phenol recovery, effluent cost and an anti-dumping duty application is underway, and the commissioning of a derivatives block is expected to move the facility towards variable cost recovery while providing a platform for forward integration into higher-margin salicylate derivatives. In formulations, the dedicated Oncology Formulation Facility at Baddi, Himachal Pradesh commenced commercial operations and received USFDA approval, EU GMP certification and ANVISA-Brazil approval during the year, with the first oncology product Bicalutamide commercialised; the general Oral Solid Dosage lines became operational for regulated markets following UK MHRA approval and EU GMP certification, and the Company is exploring toll manufacturing to raise utilisation of the specialised oncology infrastructure. The Tarapur API facility was re-approved by the USFDA and a Drug Master File for Metformin was filed with US authorities, with commercial supplies targeted post-validation. Further planned expansion includes a brownfield addition to raise antiprotozoal production capacity by 40%, incremental expansion of chloro-sulphonation facilities, incremental capacity additions and downstream product expansion in the antiprotozoal portfolio, and a greenfield project under evaluation to strengthen the speciality chemicals portfolio. On the energy side, the Company has entered into a Share Subscription and Shareholders' Agreement with Prozeal Green Power Private Limited to develop captive solar power capacity in Gujarat and Maharashtra, with planned solar and wind installations at Sarigam and Tarapur and the solar project expected to commence operations in FY 2026-27; back-pressure turbines are also planned for the co-generation power plant. Capital expenditure over the next few years is planned at Rs 300 Crores to Rs 400 Crores, directed largely towards expansion within adjoining blocks at existing sites, which the Company expects to deliver a higher asset turn than the greenfield phase.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Global scale leadership in specific molecules — largest producer of Metronidazole in India, one of the leading producers of Metformin HCl in the world, and stated global leadership in five key molecules including the Fluoroquinolones group, Tinidazole, Metronidazole Benzoate, Ketoconazole and Nimesulide
- Backward integration into key raw materials — the Sayakha methylamines facility feeds captive demand for the Metformin portfolio, reducing dependence on external suppliers and improving raw material security and cost competitiveness
- Regulatory moat — USFDA, UK MHRA, EU GMP, ANVISA and COFEPRIS approvals across named facilities, with the AR describing the industry as characterised by stringent regulatory requirements, technical expertise, high capital investments and long product development cycles
- Diversified product mix across APIs, formulations, speciality chemicals and multiple therapeutic categories, which the Company states reduces concentration risk
- Diversified client mix across geographies, regulated markets and therapeutic segments, reducing dependence on any single customer or market
- In-house R&D at two DSIR-recognised centres (Tarapur for API process development, Turbhe for complex generic formulations) with collaborations with ICT and CSIR laboratories
- Forward integration into finished dosages through wholly owned subsidiary Pinnacle Life Science, giving presence across the pharmaceutical value chain
- Adaptable multi-purpose manufacturing plants handling batch sizes from small-scale runs to multi-tonne production

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution.
